S022-01.notes: Resolved in a single, hurried paragraph after long buildup = abrupt. Distractors clearly off.

S022-02.notes: In effect only six months while being studied = provisional. 'Permanent' is the opposite; 'retroactive' and 'punitive' unsupported.

S022-03.notes: Suckers taste; arm neurons let arms respond before the brain processes the signal. A is an unsupported superlative, C contradicts, D is off-topic.

S022-04.notes: Afternoon difference with no morning difference points to the cooling effect during hot hours. B contradicts the morning data; C and D unsupported.

flags: minor: C compares 20° with only 0° and 60°, not 40°; it fully supports the claim as worded (intermediate beats both extremes), but adding 40° would make the 'highest' point explicit
S022-05.notes: Only C shows an intermediate angle beating both the smallest and the largest angles. A and B compare only two values; D is irrelevant.

S022-06.notes: Dangling modifier: the subject must be the archaeologist. D's subject is 'proposal' (possessive trap); B and C have the wrong subject.

S022-07.notes: Inverted sentence whose subject is 'two stone towers' (plural), so 'stand'. 'Stands' catches readers who take 'rim' as the subject; 'standing' gives no finite verb; 'has stood' is singular.

S022-08.notes: Adds a second advantage of recycled asphalt = Moreover. No contrast or example.

S022-09.notes: Purpose = allowed blind people to read and write by touch; only D states it.

S022-10.notes: The text gives the reason (light fades textiles) for showing a replica. The other choices are unsupported.
